China’s AI race is no longer about chatbots.

A cybersecurity agent developed by a Shanghai startup has reached a 97.28% success rate on UC Berkeley’s CyberGym benchmark.

The benchmark covers 1,507 historical vulnerabilities across 188 open-source projects and requires the agent to find flaws, construct attack inputs and verify crashes across entire codebases without external hints.

This is what happens when AI leaves the demo stage and enters the real battlefield.

Hackers are using machines.
